stem.text: A student made notes about two diseases: hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) and Lyme disease.
HFMD is caused by a viral pathogen and is transmitted in a variety of ways including:

items: ingestion of water contaminated with faeces
inhalation of droplets containing the pathogen.

stem.text: Lyme disease is caused by a bacterial pathogen and is transmitted by the bite of an infected insect.
Which statement makes a correct comparison between the diseases the student wrote about and cholera, malaria or tuberculosis (TB)?

A.text: Antibiotics can be used to kill the vector of the pathogen that causes malaria and the vector of the pathogen that causes Lyme disease.

B.text: HFMD can be transmitted in a similiar way to either cholera or TB.

C.text: The cells of the pathogen that causes HFMD and the cells of the pathogen that causes TB are prokaryotic.

D.text: Transmission of TB and HFMD could be reduced by chlorinating drinking water.
